about.title: Personal Injury Help in Needles, California
about.longDescription: Needles sits where Interstate 40 crosses the Colorado River, and that stretch of highway, along with Route 95 and Needles Highway, carries a steady flow of long-haul trucks, RVs, and local traffic. In the most recent full year on record, the city logged 16 injury collisions and 22 people hurt, with no traffic deaths reported. Small as Needles is, with under 5,000 residents, those numbers touch a lot of families here. Reports show crashes tend to cluster on Thursdays around midday, likely tied to freight schedules and errand traffic through town. If you were hurt in a collision on I-40, Route 95, or anywhere else in Needles, sorting out medical bills, missed work, and insurance calls can feel like a full-time job on top of recovering. LawProactive is a free service — not a law firm — that connects injured people with an independent personal injury attorney who can review what happened and explain your options. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover money for you. You don't have to figure this out on your own.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Soon

items.title: California's Filing Deadline
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim in California, but claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long can cost you the right to recover at all.

items.title: Shared Fault Doesn't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly responsible for the crash, you can still recover damages reduced by your share of fault. An attorney can help make sure your percentage of blame is assessed fairly.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain and suffering. That means your recovery isn't artificially boxed in by a statutory ceiling.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no retainer and no hourly bill to worry about while you're healing.

items.question: Do I have to pay anything to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney at no cost to you. If you decide to move forward, attorneys in the network work on contingency, so they only get paid if you recover compensation.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a crash in Needles?
items.answer: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government vehicle or agency was involved, the deadline can be much shorter, sometimes just six months, so it's worth checking your timeline soon.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame for the crash. Your total recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault, so partial responsibility doesn't bar you from a claim.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to happen in Needles?
items.answer: Public records show injury collisions in Needles are reported along corridors like Interstate 40 (both directions), Route 95, and Needles Highway, with activity often clustering on Thursdays between roughly noon and 2 p.m. These are neutral collision counts, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: In most ordinary personal injury cases, California does not cap non-economic damages such as pain and suffering. Your case will still depend on its specific facts, but the law doesn't impose an artificial ceiling in typical claims.
